chapter: New York, Henderson and Charlie Johnson
title: Fletcher Henderson's easygoing, easily used character
summary: Autrey felt sorry for Henderson, who went along with whatever people wanted and was taken advantage of.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving

blocks.x: From what you say, and from what I've heard, Fletcher seems to have been a rather odd person, in a way, in that --
-- for example you tell about Leora could come in and make a comment like that about the trumpet player that Fletcher thought was so great, and letting his brother steal his arrangements.

He was. He was. He was very easy, you know, he was one of those types -- I did, I felt sorry for him because he was -- well all right. Yes. Okay, you know. He's always -- always so willing to -- I'm with you, whatever you say. If that's the way you want it. Okay. Everything's all right with me. You know. And to me people took advantage of him. I think.
How had he been able to get such great bands together and keep them together, if that was the way he was (inaudible).
